caption:
65% of Indian employers plan to hire in Q4. The quarter opens next Wednesday.

That is the widest door you will see all year. And most qualified people will walk through it the same way they walk into their own Monday meetings \u2014 competent, prepared, and forgettable.

The panel is not testing your knowledge. They decided you could do the job before you sat down; that is what the shortlist was for. What they are reading in the room is bearing. Whether you fill the chair or perch on it. Whether your voice drops at the end of a sentence or climbs. Whether you can hold three seconds of silence after a hard question without rushing to fill it.

"Why you" is not an information problem. Neither is the salary number you flinch away from.

Thirty-five years of command taught Colonel Suhag one thing about high-stakes rooms: authority is demonstrated in the first ninety seconds, then confirmed or contradicted by everything after.

You have until the window closes. Use it deliberately.

topic.title: Q4 hiring window opens: India's most optimistic job market
topic.angle: For qualified people who feel overlooked internally, the Oct–Dec hiring surge is the year's highest-leverage moment — and panels, negotiations and 'why you' answers are presence problems, not competence problems.
topic.why_now: The ManpowerGroup survey shows 65% of Indian employers hiring in Oct–Dec 2026 and the quarter literally begins next Wednesday, so this hook is worthless by late October.

rationale: A stark text-only visual matches the no-nonsense command tone and lets the statistic and the presence-versus-competence distinction land without decoration.
